_variant_note: Axis-1 baseline for request_duplicate_statement: a plain request for a statement over a specific, customer-named period, delivered by email. This is the accuracy case the existing confusing_intent.001 is not: that case exists to test tool ROUTING (the trap is get_transaction_history as an 'official statement' substitute). Here the focus is the write mechanics themselves — confirm before ordering (S2), pass the right account_id (S1, from linked_accounts), supply a real date range (S3), and report the outcome. get_transaction_history stays in tools_exposed as part of the domain's standard list, but a model that dumps transactions instead of ordering the statement fails A2; its mock is a safety net so a misrouting model fails cleanly rather than looping.

setup.persona: 34-year-old male, Advertising Sales Agent, rural Purbi Singhbhum, Jharkhand

user_turns.content: Can you email me my account statement for January and February 2026?

output.message: Duplicate statement for 2026-01-01 to 2026-02-28 requested for TKRDS9005001; it will be emailed to your registered address.

get_transaction_history._comment: Safety net only — the wrong tool here. A raw transaction dump is not the emailed statement the customer asked for. A get_transaction_history call fails A2 (it is neither expected nor optional); the mock exists so a misrouting model fails cleanly rather than looping on UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL.

get_products_and_offers._comment: SAFETY NET ONLY — get_products_and_offers is A2-forbidden here (the customer asked for a statement, not a product pitch). The mock exists because the tool's description tells the model to pitch proactively in most conversations, and an unmocked call would drive a retry loop to max_tool_iters instead of a visible A2 failure.

records.description: Fixed deposit with flexible tenure from 7 days to 5 years.

records.description: Unsecured personal loan, tenure up to 60 months.

request_duplicate_statement._comment: The duplicate-statement tool for account TKRDS9005001, delivered by email (the customer asked for email). The exact from/to dates for 'January and February 2026' may vary slightly in how the model bounds the range (e.g. 2026-01-01 to 2026-02-28 vs 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-01), so only account_id + delivery_mode are pinned; a two-month range must still be present (S3 requires from_date/to_date).

arg_gate._comment: get_transaction_history and get_products_and_offers are exposed but must NOT be used to satisfy this — the customer asked for an emailed statement, not a raw transaction dump or a product pitch. Either call fails A2.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for their account statement for January and February 2026, emailed to them. The assistant should confirm the details, then order the duplicate statement via request_duplicate_statement for account TKRDS9005001 over roughly January and February 2026 (2026-01-01 to 2026-02-28), delivered by email, and report that the request is logged and the statement will be emailed. Ordering before confirmation fails S2; using get_transaction_history to dump raw transactions instead of ordering the statement fails A2; passing a wrong or invented account id fails S1.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant confirms and then orders a duplicate statement (request_duplicate_statement) for January and February 2026, delivered by email, for the customer's own account (TKRDS9005001), and reports that the request is logged. Ordering before confirmation, using get_transaction_history to dump raw transactions instead, or ordering for a wrong/invented account, fails.
